_comment: [OPUS-4.8] sq-v3nel (2026-07-07): feature-OFF wasm-bundle CHANGE DECLARATION.
The vectorized-feature-off gate (leg 2, .github/workflows/vectorized-feature-off.yml)
builds the feature-OFF wasm bundle TWICE in one CI run — once from the base
(target-branch/merge-base) tree and once from the head (PR/merged) tree — and compares
them byte-for-byte. Same toolchain + same run => deterministic, with NO static byte pin,
so NO merge-order dependence (this replaces the retired feature_off_exact pin — see the
retirement entry in bench/perf-baseline.json's _comment chain).
POLICY: a PR that INTENTIONALLY changes always-compiled engine/core code in a way that
moves the feature-OFF bundle bytes MUST DECLARE it by INCREMENTING "change_token" below
(by 1) in the same reviewed diff, and add a dated rationale line to this _comment. A PR
that does NOT touch always-compiled feature-OFF code leaves the token alone: its build is
byte-identical to base and passes automatically. An accidental default-path/vectorized
byte change with an un-bumped token FAILS the gate — that is the whole point.
SCOPE: this token governs INTENT (did you mean to change the feature-OFF bytes at all?).
The SIZE of an accepted change is governed SEPARATELY, unchanged, by the
metrics.wasm_bundle_bytes floor ratchet (+/-2% band) in bench/perf-baseline.json /
bench.yml. A change moving the bundle > +/-2% must ALSO raise that floor.
WHY A DEDICATED FILE (not a field in perf-baseline.json): scripts/perf-gate.py's
auto-ratchet-down rewrite (write_baseline) reconstructs each metric with only
floor/threshold/mode and would silently WIPE any extra field on the next push-to-main
improvement commit. WHY A TOKEN (not a PR-body marker): a PR-body line is invisible in
merge_group events (the merged commit set has no single PR body) and is not part of the
reviewed diff; a token bump is audit-visible and least-gameable.
change_token seeded at 0. Increment by exactly 1 per declared feature-OFF byte change.
